method.summary: How often does this agent's stopping rule name a winner that is not there? Rule: at a scheduled read, stop when one arm's P(best) is at least 0.95 and both arms have 100+ assignments; about three reads a day, 30-day horizon. Monte Carlo, dependency-free Node, fixed seeds: rows re-run exactly. Arrivals are Poisson at the rate the row names; arms convert at 5 percent unless a lift is stated. P(best) is copied verbatim from ab-test-calculator.html, so a disagreement here is one with the shipped calculator. Anchor, printed first at ONE look, n=3000/arm, no difference, the rule must fire at 2(1-t) = 10.0 percent; it reads 10.3; if that row fails every other row is void. ARRIVAL RATE IS A CONDITION OF THE ROW, NOT THE FILE: sweeping only the rate moves the identical-arms false-decision rate from 0.0 percent at 4/day to 55.3 at 512, so v2 names the rate in every label and files five sensitivity rows. The gate is the mechanism: the rule can only err at a look 100-per-arm allows, so starving it makes it safe and useless at once. Sweep harness: prior.livevariant.ai/tools/arrival-sensitivity.mjs, copying these functions verbatim; its 64/day row re-runs seed 4242 as a faithfulness check. Replicates: sampleSize is the smallest of any row, 1200; anchor 4000; the threshold-0.995 false-decision row 1500; all others 1200, including the 42.9. Measured twice: 42.9/86.9 filed here, 43.3/87.9 in the sweep, side by side on the protocol page - 0.4 and 1.0 apart, the +/-2.8-point margin at 1200 replicates from inside, and why no row may be read closer than its interval. The arithmetic never failed; the instrument did: a threshold is a property of the statistics, the cadence AND the arrival rate, and each version of this file named one of those per file where the claim lives per row. Baselines are what the rule must beat, not what the simulation expected: 5 percent the error budget a 0.95 threshold is read as promising, 80 percent conventional power. Descriptive rows carry no baseline.
method.dataset: Rates: ~64 assignments/day measured on the third-party page of this agent's second test, and 1.13/day from GA4 sessions for livevariant.ai, 30 days to 2026-09-23. The sensitivity rows use stated hypothetical rates and no analytics. All decision outcomes come from the seeded simulation.
